title: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

sense.text:
“Whom shall he teach knowledge?” A lot of men proclaim themselves ministers of God. A lot of teachers, priests, prophets and pastors will say, ‘I understand the Bible, join my church, I teach the Word of God correctly.’ But this is what God says: whom is God going to teach the knowledge of his scriptures, and “whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Whom is he going to make to understand his law and his Bible?

The knowledge is the law, and the doctrine is the law. What Israel United in Christ teaches is the law, statutes and commandments in the faith of the Messiah. That is what makes the Israelites so dangerous: the law through the faith of Christ is what is going to get our people redeemed. That is what is going to change our people, fix the family, fix the black man and fix the black woman: God’s law.

He teaches “them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” The milk is the basics. The most important thing when you come in is to understand the laws. People come and ask what to do: learn the laws and learn to apply them in your life. Don’t worry about the prophecies and the mysteries right now; you will learn that eventually. When you first come in it is all about the milk, just like a newborn baby needs milk for nourishment, and two or three years later he gets teeth and can start chewing solid food. The milk is how do I have to behave, how do I have to walk, how do I have to talk, what does God require of me: putting aside evil, hypocrisy and malice.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” People in the streets say, ‘All you Israelites do is jump from one part of the Bible to another part.’ They don’t understand Isaiah 28. The Bible teaches us here a little in the Old Testament, there a little in the New Testament, here a little in the Apocrypha. The Bible is not written in chronological order, and even Jeremiah, as we go through the topic, is not in order: it jumps. These are records that we are reading, and that is why precept must be upon precept.

precepts.why: What is the knowledge? “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law.” God compares his knowledge to the law: God’s knowledge is the law. So when Isaiah asks whom God will teach knowledge, he is asking who God is going to make to understand his law, to understand his Bible.

What is the doctrine? Is the doctrine of the Bible that God loves all races and everybody can be one in Jesus? God says, “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” Once again the law, the law, the law. The doctrine Isaiah speaks of is God’s law, and it is the law through the faith of Christ that is going to get our people redeemed.

Them that are weaned from the milk are the ones God makes to understand doctrine. Peter says, “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk”, and before that, “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile.” Malice is evil intent, and it fills our hearts and minds, us black people and Hispanic people: there is malice in us, hatred, jealousy, fornication, adultery. We have to lay it aside, along with the hypocrisy, “and envies, and all evil speakings.”

Read the comments on the YouTube videos: Israel United in Christ gets a lot of hate and evil speech, and it is black people and Hispanic people hating their own brothers for doing the work. That is not going to stop us; it only adds fuel, and we need more haters. Black man, we have to learn to put aside hypocrisy, guile, hatred and evil speaking, and we put it away by practicing keeping the commandments. That is the milk God is speaking of in Isaiah 28: learning how to behave, walk and talk the way God requires.

“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof.” We must give our mind to the law of the Most High. Most of us came from the Christian Church, some from the Catholic Church, some even about to be deacons there, but a lot of us were not occupied in the Bible, and those who were reading could never understand. We are supposed to be occupied in the scriptures, occupied in the Old Testament and in the New Testament: when we get off work we read the scriptures, when we get home we read. That is why we read four chapters a day, so that in one year we read the whole Bible.

Such a man “will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” “He will keep the sayings of the renowned men”, and where subtle parables are, “he will be there also.” In the Bible there are parables, dark sentences and hard things to understand. “He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.”

Who does God reveal that to? Not the Christian ministers. It is the Israelites, the ones that keep the commandments, who are able to bring the understanding to the people. That is the man who gets the precept upon precept.

Are the secrets of the Bible revealed to everybody? No, only to the prophets. “Surely the Lord God will do nothing”, but he reveals “his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The heavenly Father, the creator of heaven and earth, has secrets, and those secrets are in the Bible.

How do we learn those secrets? By what we read earlier: studying, applying the laws, precept upon precept, being occupied in the meditation thereof, addicting ourselves to the scriptures.

“Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee, that he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.” Favoured is the man the Most High chooses and causes to approach unto him.

That is what we want: to be favoured by the Most High and brought closer to him. Sometimes it feels cold, and you ask why the Lord is dealing with you, what is wrong with you. It’s sin. The Most High brings us closer to him as we keep his commandments, as we continue to have faith, and as we are occupied in the meditation thereof.

sense.text: This is a harder side to understand: the Bible speaks of something called regeneration, and it ties to the title of the class, history repeats itself. “The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem”: this is King Solomon.

“What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?” Whether you are cutting wood, doing brickwork or painting, all the labour, the sweating, the work you put in: what profit do you get out of that? Solomon is painting a picture, and we have to visualize what he is telling us.

“One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh.” Examine a generation of people, seventy or eighty years, the years God says we live. The father and the mother have children, eventually the father and mother pass away, the children get older: one generation comes and another passes on. “But the earth abideth for ever.”

The first question asked of the bishop, on first coming to this truth, was whether the world was going to be destroyed by planet Nibiru, Planet X, the conspiracy theory that it would crash into the earth. Before coming to the truth there was an uncle teaching about the Illuminati, saying the white man is the devil, there will be concentration camps, don’t get the chip. Taking that back to high school in New York only got the question, ‘What the hell is wrong with you?’ There was no profit and no solution in it.

When the Bible is our foundation we can’t be moved; the Bible answers all questions. Conspiracy theories are research upon research, one scholar or one crackhead putting an article together. Some of them are true, and we know because the Bible confirms it, but a lot of them you take with a grain of salt. Israel uses the Bible to filter everything: is this right? Does God say it? That’s how we roll. The Bible says the earth abides for ever.

“The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.” The wind goes toward the south “and turneth about unto the north”, and “the wind returneth again according to his circuits.” “All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.” It’s all a cycle.
“All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.” Solomon goes deep: we always want more, and it can never be enough.

“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” There it is: Solomon is letting us know history repeats itself. There is no new thing under the sun; it all comes back again and happens again.

Everything has a cycle, and generations have a cycle, meaning we have all been here before. A lot of us have returned. Solomon used nature as the example, the rivers, the sun and the generations that come and go, and compared our spirits coming back to this earth to that cycle of life. This is regeneration, and it is what deja vu is: the feeling that one has lived through the present situation before is Ecclesiastes 1, the spirit having been here before. The world has questions it cannot answer, why our life is messed up, why black people are always on the bottom, why so many churches with one Bible, but the Bible explains everything, and that is what draws us to this truth.

The world calls it historic recurrence, the rise and fall of empires, and their author Mark Twain wrote that no occurrence is sole and solitary but a repetition of a thing which has happened before. Solomon already said that. These are Esau’s scholars, wise men, authors, psychologists and think tanks, trying to explain what the Bible already explains.

So it is with Babylon. The Babylonian Empire led by Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Israel, and America did the same thing, and as Babylon was eventually destroyed, so will America be. During Babylon Jeremiah prophesied and taught Israel to repent, for destruction was coming from the north, and that is the message we tell our people. America is in the Holy Bible. The prophets wrote this thousands of years ago, and now we are living it: the prophecy back then is becoming our history now.
“Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.”

“There is no remembrance of former things.” When your spirit comes back in this earth you do not remember the life you lived when you were here before. You think everything is new, that this is the first time you’ve been here, but you’ve been here before, Solomon says.

precepts.why: God speaks to his people through all their generations: “Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb: And even to your old age I am he”, carrying the older brothers and the older sisters. “I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.”

“Remember this”, God says to his people, “O ye transgressors.” “Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me.” The Most High is taking credit: there is nobody you can compare to his power.

“Declaring the end from the beginning”: from the time of Genesis God already declared what is going to happen in the end, “and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.” So in the Bible you can read what happened in the beginning and what is going to happen in the end, and as you read you see that a lot of what is happening now has happened before, and a lot of the spirits that were here back then are back today.

So the message to the black man is to repent. That is the same message Jeremiah gave the people in Babylon’s day: regardless of how comfortable you may be, if you don’t keep God’s commandments you will be consumed with destruction by King Nebuchadnezzar. We say the same: if our people don’t repent, they will be consumed by World War 3.

Esau tries to explain regeneration. How does God describe Esau? “They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them”, and the heart “is deep.” This is Esau, the wicked: their minds think deep, thirty to seventy years ahead. These are think tanks. God says this is the race he made.

So Esau writes of historic recurrence, the repetition of similar events in history and the rise and fall of empires, and his scholars and psychologists try to explain human behavior. They understand that things really happen over and over again, but the Bible already explained it in Ecclesiastes 1.

sense.text:
To understand the Babylonian Empire: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers.” The watchers are the angels of God. “And the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.” Over the kingdoms he sets up even the lowest of men.

God gives the kingdom to whomsoever he will. In America it was of the Most High to set up Donald Trump, of God to set up Barack Obama, of God to set up George Bush. God gets the credit.

When you read the book of Jeremiah it is the rise of Nebuchadnezzar II, the rise of the Babylonian Empire. Before it was the Assyrian Empire, and there was Assyrian and Egyptian influence on our people in education, religion and politics. Then a new empire emerged, Babylon, the neo-Babylonian empire of the time of Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel, and we were conquered and inside it, and Babylon eventually conquered Egypt. The Most High gave Babylon that kingdom.

precepts.why: “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The king’s mind is in the hand of the Lord. The president, the kings, the dignitaries: all these men, their minds are in the hands of the Most High. That is how the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whomsoever he will.

God takes credit for everything, and we always have to give all praises to the Most High. “For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion.” He sets rulers over every people, but we belong to the Most High God.

sense.text:
“The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.” This gives Jeremiah’s tribe. Jeremiah was a Levite, of the priests: the Haitians. This is his people.

Jeremiah prophesied as Babylon was rising. Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, was completely destroyed in Jeremiah’s time, by the Babylonians allied with the Medes, and Babylon was getting power. Nineveh was the greatest city in the world at that time, the way America is the greatest and most powerful country in the world in our time, with 800 military bases throughout the world and 37% of its finances spent on weapons and war, when other countries spend 11% or 9%. That is all they are about, weapons and war: that is Esau’s blessing, to be blessed with the art of war and conquering.

“To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.” Jeremiah was during the time of King Josiah.

At the battle of Carchemish, Assyria joined with Egypt to fight against Babylon, and they lost, because God prophesied that Babylon would be a world empire. Josiah tried to get involved and fight the Egyptian pharaoh Necho, and Necho told him his fight was not against him: God had sent him to fight against the king of Babylon. Josiah did not listen, and Josiah got killed.

“It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah king of Judah.” Jeremiah was during the time of King Jehoiakim and also during the time of King Zedekiah, “unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

So the kings during Jeremiah’s ministry were Josiah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim and Zedekiah. Jehoahaz is the one king this chapter does not mention, because he was only king for three months.

precepts.why:
The one king Jeremiah 1 does not mention is Jehoahaz: “Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.” “And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.”

“And Pharaoh–nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver”: the Egyptians were taxing Israel.

“And Pharaoh–nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim.” This is the history of how Jehoiakim was made king. He was placed as king by the Egyptian pharaoh, set up as a vassal king, meaning ‘you’re gonna do whatever I tell you’: a puppet. It is like today, when America goes to different countries and sets up puppet rulers who are not really for the people; they are there on behalf of American policies, and that is all they are there for. It was the same thing with Jehoiakim: Pharaoh Necho set him up as a vassal king, “and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.”

sense.text: This is where Jeremiah speaks about Jehoahaz. “Weep ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him: but weep sore for him that goeth away: for he shall return no more, nor see his native country.” He is talking about King Jehoahaz, who was taken away to Egypt.

“For thus saith the Lord touching Shallum the son of Josiah king of Judah, which reigned instead of Josiah his father”: Shallum is Jehoahaz. “He shall not return thither any more: But he shall die in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more.”

“Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour’s service without wages, and giveth him not for his work.” That is what Jehoahaz was doing to the people: “I will build me a wide house and large chambers, and cutteth him out windows; and it is cieled with cedar, and painted with vermilion.”

He did not follow the example of his father, King Josiah. “Shalt thou reign, because thou closest thyself in cedar? did not thy father eat and drink, and do judgment and justice, and then it was well with him? He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well with him: was not this to know me? saith the Lord.”

“And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Sihor?” Sihor is a river in Egypt. “Or what hast thou to do in the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the river?”

He is not talking about literally drinking from the river, even though we did get the natural resources from these lands, because Israel was in these areas. He is talking about learning from the Egyptians and the Assyrians: our people wanting to learn from the other nations, namely Assyria and Egypt. Before Babylon rose, the influences on our people in education, religion and politics were Assyria and Egypt.
“Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee: know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God.”

precepts.why:
“But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” Israel became mingled among the heathen and learned the works of the other nations. We don’t want to serve God; we serve the idols of the other nations: “And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.”

That is the same thing that happened in Babylon, and the same thing that happened here in America. When we came here we learned Christianity, we learned Christmas, we learned Thanksgiving. These are not God’s holidays; these are days set up by America. Thanksgiving is in honor of slaughtering the Native American Indians. We learned these traditions, the same as in the time of Jeremiah, when Jeremiah was prophesying against Israel.

sense.text:
This is before the temple was completely obliterated. Jeremiah prophesied that an evil was coming from the north and Jerusalem would be destroyed, and Israel said ‘yeah, whatever’. Israel hated Jeremiah for that.

“Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart.” Circumcision is where you cut the foreskin off the penis, and circumcision is the law the Most High gave to us. But circumcising yourselves to the Lord means we have to change our minds and cut our ties with this country. Thanksgiving, we have to cut it out; Christmas, Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, we have to cut them out. That is the circumcision he is referring to.

Literal circumcision is still the law, and that daggone thing hurt. Coming into the church uncircumcised, it had to be done; you couldn’t walk, you had to walk slow to class. But it is the covenant in Genesis between us and the Most High, a covenant in the flesh. Brothers, if you are not circumcised, get circumcised; don’t be scared.

“Ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem”: by this time much of the northern kingdom, the Hispanic tribes, the Indian tribes, the Native Americans, had been taken away by Assyria and placed throughout its cities, thousands upon thousands, in places like Nineveh and Carchemish. Very few remnants of the north were left. So the land of Israel was Judah, Benjamin and Levi. Judah is the tribe of Judah, which today are the American blacks; the inhabitants of Jerusalem are Benjamin, the West Indian blacks, and Levi, the Haitians.

“Lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.”

“Declare ye in Judah”: God says to Jeremiah, declare in Judah and publish in Jerusalem. “Blow ye the trumpet in the land”: that is a sound preparing for war. “Cry, gather together, and say, Assemble yourselves, and let us go into the defenced cities.”

“Set up the standard toward Zion”, set up the banner toward Zion: “retire, stay not: for I will bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.” God told Jeremiah to prophesy to his people that, for all the evil they did, he was bringing an evil from the north to destroy his people. That evil and great destruction is Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army.

Israel looked at Jeremiah and said, you’re a rebel, you don’t love your people, you hate us, we’re gonna kill you for telling us that. But that is what God told Jeremiah to do: have no fear, tell them this message.

“The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”: on his way to Jerusalem. God declares the end from the beginning and reveals his secrets to the prophets, so Jeremiah was instructed to tell Israel that God would destroy them. And as you read on, he gives instructions: even though I’m gonna destroy you, if you humble down to the king of Babylon I will have mercy on you, but if you rebel against the king of Babylon, I’ma jack you up. “He is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

History repeats itself. What happened in the time of Jeremiah is happening in this time: the correlations between Babylon and what they did to us and America and what they did to us, and between how Jeremiah taught Israel what to do in order to be delivered and what we are teaching our people to do in order to be delivered.

“For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness.” From the least of our people to the greatest of our people. Today the least of our people are the regular citizens, the regular brothers just going to work, and the greatest are those who hold high political positions and high titles in office. In that time it was from the least of the Israelites, the poor Israelites, to the priests: “from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.”
“They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.”

“Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush.” You are supposed to be ashamed of your sins. To blush is to be shamefaced, shy. God says my people were not shy, neither could they blush; they were not ashamed of the sins they were committing.

An example is in the protests going on right now. They are protesting for their rights, to end brutality, to be treated equal and fairly, but God says our people will be oppressed. This is supposed to be a protest for our people being beat down by the cops, tired of oppression, and what the hell does LGBT shaking it behind in front of the cops have to do with oppression? That is what the scripture means: our people do not even feel a shame for some of the sins they are involved in. Benjamin, we don’t roll like that; that ain’t us.

The woman who was so ashamed that she washed Christ’s feet with her tears knew she was guilty of sins worthy of death. God says not our people: they are not ashamed, neither could they blush. “Therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.”

“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.” Israel was not listening; they were rebelling against Jeremiah.
These are other sins they were doing. “For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the Lord: they have set their abominations in the house which is called by my name, to pollute it.”

“And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire.” We were burning our sons and daughters in the fire: child sacrifice. Tophet was a location in Jerusalem, in Gehenna, where worshippers influenced by the ancient Canaanite religion sacrificed children to the gods Moloch and Baal by burning them alive. Gehenna, the valley of Hinnom, was where some of the kings of Judah sacrificed their children by fire, and thereafter it was deemed cursed. Tophet became a symbol for hell within Christendom.

This is the evil our people were doing: killing their children. Does that happen today? Yes it does. Thousands of black women abort thousands of babies in the name of white Jesus and then go to church on Sunday. Brothers kill each other in Chicago and New Orleans, and one black woman alone may have had six abortions, but it is legal, because America says she has the right to do that. God says you don’t have that right. Because of the evil they were doing, God was going to bring evil from the north.

It is like the scene in Game of Thrones where the witch told Stannis Baratheon that for him to receive more power he had to sacrifice his daughter, and he burned his daughter alive. “Which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

“Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place.” A lot of dead bodies would be there because of the destruction coming from Nebuchadnezzar.

“And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.” “Then will I cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride”: all of that is going to cease, “for the land shall be desolate.”

precepts.why:
This is what Jeremiah was teaching: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” That throne frames mischief by laws: it allows sin through legality. Through the law you can commit an abortion; it is legal, and certain states say you can do it at two months, three months, four months, five months. Esau says, we’re telling you, you got the right to kill that baby.

So who are you going to follow, God or the white man? God says you are a murderer; that is murder. They try to water the term down and call it abortion. No: it is child sacrifice, the same burning of sons and daughters done at Tophet.

sense.text: This is where the opposition against Jeremiah starts. “Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things”: he heard that Jeremiah was prophesying against Jerusalem. He had power and a position.
“Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet”: he smacked him in the face, “and put him in the stocks”, put him in jail, “that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.”

“Behold, I will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon”: this is Nebuchadnezzar, “and he shall carry them captive into Babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.”

“Moreover I will deliver all the strength of this city, and all the labours thereof, and all the precious things thereof, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah will I give into the hand of their enemies.” We had treasures, we had our own land, we had wealth. But God told Jeremiah to tell our forefathers that evil was coming from the north, that they would be destroyed and there would be no voice of mirth or gladness. It is the same thing Moses told our people, and Israel did not believe Moses.

“And thou, Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house shall go into captivity: and thou shalt come to Babylon, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buried there, thou, and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.” Pashur was teaching lies.

“O Lord, thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived”, Jeremiah said. “I am in derision daily, every one mocketh me.” “Because the word of the Lord was made a reproach unto me, and a derision, daily.” They put Jeremiah in jail for teaching the word of God, for saying what was right.

“Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” Jeremiah said, for this I’m not even gonna speak of the Most High no more. “But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” The word of God was in his bones as a fire; he could not keep his mouth closed. He had to teach Israel what they were doing; he had to prophesy that Israel was wicked as hell.

“For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” “All my familiars watched for my halting”: the people in his circle wanted to see Jeremiah fall, “saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.”

This is the same thing we went through as a congregation. There were wicked Israelites who wanted to see Israel United in Christ fall, wanted the whole movement destroyed, wanted to see evil come on us. But we have only been growing: the Bishop is doing five radio shows, and there are congregations in Africa and throughout the West Indian islands. You cannot stop this truth. One of them went on the BBC documentary and called IUIC a hate group. Did he say how often IUIC paid his rent, how often IUIC helped them? No. God is showing us there will be wicked Israelites who don’t believe, and Israelites who are serious about this work. Jeremiah went through the same thing: Pashur smacked him in the face and put him in jail.

This Pashur is “the son of Melchiah”, and he is not the same man as the other Pashur, the son of Immer. That other Pashur was against Jeremiah: he put his hands on Jeremiah and had him arrested, showing you he had power and he had a position. This one is sent by king Zedekiah to Jeremiah, with Zephaniah the priest, to enquire of the Lord.

“Enquire, I pray thee, of the Lord for us; for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon maketh war against us.” Remember the history: Nebuchadnezzar came against Jerusalem three times. The first time, 605 BC, he took Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael and sent them to Babylon with the other Israelites; Jews were deported. The second time, around 598, 597, he took Ezekiel the prophet; he did not destroy the city by this time, but he took Jews and took us back to Babylon. The third time he completely destroyed the temple and Jerusalem, took thousands of Israelites out of their homeland, and only left the poor Israelites in the land.

The map of the three waves shows him coming the first time from the north and going down toward Gaza, and that is when Daniel and those other Israelites were taken back to Babylon. After the war with Egypt, Nebuchadnezzar set up his own vassal kings in Jerusalem, and Zedekiah was one of them. And the black arrow on the map is Esau: Esau assisted the Babylonians in the destruction. So when we read “Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon maketh war against us”, by this time he is already coming back.

We are slowly going through the Babylonian Empire, and then we are going to deal with what happened to our people here in America.

Jeremiah answers them: this is what you should tell king Zedekiah. “Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands”, “And I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm, even in anger, and in fury, and in great wrath.”

Do you hear it? God is saying, I am going to fight against you. Understand that during slavery time, brothers and sisters, God was against us. God did not hear our prayers. God was against us, and the reason is that we have been punished, brothers and sisters, throughout Saudi Arabia, Africa, the eastern hemisphere, Thailand: we have been punished for committing iniquity.

“I will smite the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast: they shall die of a great pestilence.” Then the Lord will deliver Zedekiah, his servants and the people that are left “from the pestilence, from the sword, and from the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon”.

The famine is because they besieged Jerusalem, meaning no food, no water. And what did we begin to do? We started eating our children, eating our wives. That is what Deuteronomy 28 was explaining. Into the hand of their enemies, “he shall smite them with the edge of the sword; he shall not spare them, neither have pity, nor have mercy.”

“Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.” That is what we are telling our people today: we are setting before you the way of life, and the way of life is through God’s laws. The way of death is, you can do whatever you want, you can break God’s commandments, but you will die when destruction comes to America.

“He that abideth in this city shall die by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.” Many were rebelling against king Nebuchadnezzar. They did not want to listen; they were going to fight against him and try to stay in the city, and God told Jeremiah to tell Israel they are going to die by the sword. “But he that goeth out, and falleth to the Chaldeans”, the one that goes out and submits himself to the Chaldeans, “he shall live, and his life shall be unto him for a prey.”

precepts.why:
Brothers, you have to realize we are God’s chosen people, and that is why we are being punished. When God says “I myself will fight against you”, it is not that he has thrown us away: “For the Lord will not cast off for ever: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.”

Though he causes grief, yet will he have compassion. Right now a lot of our people are grieved; they are in pain. Look at what happened in California: a man hung by a tree, and they ruled it a suicide. A lot of our people are tired of the pain of the oppression, but they must realize they have to return to the Most High God. That is the only option we have: we have to return to this Bible, and we have to keep the Most High God’s commandments.

sense.text:
The Most High gives Jeremiah a parable to tell Israel. “The Lord shewed me, and, behold, two baskets of figs were set before the temple of the Lord”, after Nebuchadrezzar had carried away captive Jeconiah king of Judah, with “the princes of Judah, with the carpenters and smiths, from Jerusalem”.

Jeconiah was another king of Judah, and he went by more than one name. He ruled real briefly, about three months, and he was dethroned by the king of Babylon. That is just to give you the history.

“One basket had very good figs, even like the figs that are first ripe: and the other basket had very naughty figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.” The Lord asks Jeremiah what he sees: “Figs; the good figs, very good; and the evil, very evil, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.”

When you read on down, he gives the example of the other figs, the evil and naughty ones. These are the Israelites that rebelled against Babylon, that did not listen to Jeremiah, and guess who is in this bunch: Zedekiah.

“Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge them that are carried away captive of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good.” Carried away for their good means the Most High showed mercy to these Israelites. This is Daniel, this is Ezekiel, these are the other captives that were taken out of the land for their good.

It shows you the Most High had mercy on some of our people that were enslaved. He shows mercy to some, and to others he does not show mercy.

“For I will set mine eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them again to this land: and I will build them, and not pull them down; and I will plant them, and not pluck them up.” And he will give them “an heart to know me, that I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.”

This is where it gets controversial; this is where it gets heated between Jeremiah and Israel because of what he is prophesying. Put yourself in the time of Jeremiah. Israel is being rebellious, but they are looking at Jeremiah like, you really don’t care about your own people. How can you say we are going to be destroyed? How can you say we are going to be killed by the king of Babylon, and you want us to submit to him and not fight back? So in their mind, we need to kill him. But Jeremiah says no: this message that I am telling you is what the Most High told me to tell you. Humble down and submit.

The Lord tells Jeremiah, “Stand in the court of the Lord’s house”, the temple, and speak to all that come to worship there “all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word”.

“If so be they will hearken, and turn every man from his evil way”. That has always been the message from the prophets: to listen, and to turn from the evil way, “that I may repent me of the evil, which I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings.”

“If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you, To hearken to the words of my servants the prophets”. See what the Most High is saying: if we will not listen and walk in his law, what is going to happen?

It is the same today. A lot of celebrities have been sharing our content. A Christian gospel singer responded to us and shared the video of what we did in Chicago, thousands of us marching. On the comment board you see some of our people: ‘they hate black women, they hate us, they hate their own people.’ And you see other people responding, ‘these brothers are for real, these brothers in purple and gold are serious.’ But you always get a lot of our people saying they hate us, they are against us, because we are telling our people God’s law and they are taking it as hatred. It is the same thing Jeremiah went through.

“Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.” When Jeremiah had made an end of speaking, “the priests and the prophets and all the people took him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.” They grabbed Jeremiah: kill him, kill him, get rid of him. “Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh”?

That is the same reaction we get when we are teaching in Queens, in Brooklyn, in Kansas, in Chicago, in New Orleans. Our people look at us like, wait, what are y’all talking about, God is going to kill us, we are going to be destroyed? They grabbed Jeremiah and said, we are going to put this man to death.

“When the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king’s house”, and “Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die”. The priests and the prophets are against Jeremiah, while the princes of Judah and the people are considering what Jeremiah is saying. There is a division among the people: Jeremiah might be telling us the truth, versus the priests and the prophets saying no, he needs to be put to death.

Now Jeremiah speaks to the princes and to the people: “The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city”. He tells them the same thing he told them before: “amend your ways and your doings, and obey the voice of the Lord your God; and the Lord will repent him of the evil that he hath pronounced against you.”

“As for me, behold, I am in your hand”: whatever you want to do to me, that is on you, but I am telling you what God told me. “But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof”.

Christ told us this. When you examine the history, it was our people that killed the prophets. That is why we cannot seek love; we have to teach as it is written, because the Bible prophesied a remnant shall return. So you online, you listening, you have to decide within yourself: am I that remnant? Is it time for me to return? I have been watching online for four years and I have not fellowshipped. I need to make a decision. I need to get involved and do this work, and assist however I can.

“This man is not worthy to die: for he hath spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God.” The princes and the people listened to Jeremiah: he is saying the right thing. That happens to us in the street. Sometimes you get some of our people that say, this is true, what these brothers are saying is true, and you get a majority of our people saying these brothers have got to go. But look here: the Most High moved the spirits of the princes and the people to consider what Jeremiah was saying, and to say, he is right.

Certain of the elders of the land rose up and reminded the people of Micah the Morasthite, the Micah from the book of Micah, who prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah: “Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.” That is what Micah taught in those days.

The princes and the people are reminding the prophets and the priests. The prophets and the priests need to be reminded: what the hell is this? It goes to show you that during the time of Jeremiah there were a lot of false prophets, saying ‘peace, peace’ when God says there is no peace. It is the same thing today. Christian ministers and political leaders say we shall have peace, we can work with America, all we have to do is vote, just vote and a change will come one day. In other words, eventually there will be peace. But that is not what God says.

“Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the Lord”? Hezekiah did not kill Micah, and the Lord repented of the evil. “Thus might we procure great evil against our souls”: if we kill Jeremiah, we bring great evil against our souls.

There was also a man that prophesied in the name of the Lord, Urijah, “who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah”. King Jehoiakim heard what this prophet said, and “the king sought to put him to death: but when Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt”. Jehoiakim sent men into Egypt to go get the prophet so he could kill him, and they brought him to the king, “who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.”

See that? King Jehoiakim killed one of the prophets of the Most High. This is our people. This is our own race.

But the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah: that brother was with Jeremiah, “that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.” The Most High said he would do something for Jeremiah.

precepts.why:
This is where the Most High said he would do something for Jeremiah: “Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.” That is why a man was with Jeremiah when the people sought his life.

That is a message to us. As long as we stay true to the Most High’s word, the Most High may have our enemies show mercy on us. It depends on who we are. Urijah: the Most High did not have mercy on him; it was meant for Urijah to be put to death. Jeremiah was not meant to be taken to Babylon like Daniel and Ezekiel; Jeremiah was meant to stay. The Most High has different situations happen for different people, different brothers, different prophets.

Nevertheless, for some of us he will have our enemies show mercy on us, as long as we stay true and faithful. He does promise this thing: the enemy will entreat you well.

sense.text:
We are now getting close to 587 BC, when the Babylonians completely destroyed the temple. Jeremiah was one of the Levites, and Levi was scattered throughout the different areas; look at how Israel treats him in his own land. “Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city”, “for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt.”

It came off as if Jeremiah was not about his race, but in fact he really was; he was just telling them the truth. That is how it is today. It comes off that these Israelites don’t really care about black brothers, about black women. But we do. We are telling you what the Most High says, whether it hurts your feelings or not. ‘Have I become your enemy because I tell you the truth?’ That is how Israel took Jeremiah’s message: he does not seek the welfare of his people, but their hurt.

Ebed-melech “took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.” By this time they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon and barely fed him. He is malnourished, he is not being fed, so Ebed-melech the Ethiopian tells him, “Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords”: put the rags under your armpits and hold on so you can come up. “So they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon”, malnourished, climbing up out of the dungeon.

“Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him”, “I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.” When you read the chapters earlier, Zedekiah put Jeremiah in prison, and he put him there because he knew the people who did not like Jeremiah wanted to kill him. Now Zedekiah is coming to Jeremiah privately and speaking to him.

“If I declare it unto thee, wilt thou not surely put me to death?” Aren’t you still going to kill me? And Zedekiah “sware secretly unto Jeremiah” that he would not put him to death.

“If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house”. Humble yourself, Zedekiah, to the king of Babylon. That is all Zedekiah had to do: listen, and the city would not be burned with fire. But he did not obey Jeremiah’s words. “But if thou wilt not go forth”, the city shall be given to the Chaldeans, “and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.”

“And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews”. What did he say? I am afraid of the Jews. Zedekiah was afraid of the people, of what they were going to think of him. It goes to show you what kind of king he was. At the end of the day David stood by the Most High’s word; even in his mistakes he still stayed faithful. Zedekiah’s decisions were based on appeasing the people.

That is not the type of leaders we have to be. We have to always remain faithful to the Most High. That is why we are in the street even though Israel is coming against it. ‘Why do you teach so rough? Why do you scream so loud?’ Because that is what the Most High says; we follow whatever the Most High tells us.

Jeremiah answers, “They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the Lord”: obey the voice of the Most High, “so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.”

“But if thou refuse to go forth”: if you refuse, Zedekiah, to humble yourself to the king of Babylon, all the women left in the king’s house shall be brought out, and “they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.”

This is talking about 587, 586 BC, when they completely annihilated the city and the temple that Solomon built, took all the Jews out, and only left the poor of the land.

“Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.” If the princes come and ask, Jeremiah is to say, “I presented my supplication before the king”. The princes came and asked him, and he told them as the king commanded, “So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not perceived.” The Jews never perceived what the conversation was between Zedekiah and Jeremiah. “So Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken”.

Chapter 39 is Jerusalem destroyed: Babylon annihilates Jerusalem. This is the final destruction, and the final destruction means the destruction of the temple.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem, “and they besieged it.” When you read it, they besieged Jerusalem between eighteen and thirty months. That’s damn near two years, no food, no water. That’s where you get the Book of Lamentations, and that’s where you get Deuteronomy 28 being fulfilled on our people: people eating each other.

“The city was broken up.” Imagine the siege: no food for a year, a year and a half, two years. You can say ‘I would never eat somebody’, but try having no food for a year and a half. This is what a lot of Israelites were doing, eating each other. Could you imagine looking at your own child as a piece of chicken? This is what our people came down to: they started to eat the flesh of their own children, husbands eating their wives.

Zedekiah tried to run. He saw the princes of Babylon in the gate and fled with the men of war “out of the city by night”, but the Chaldeans “overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.” The map of the deportations of the Jews shows it: Nebuchadnezzar came three times, and Zedekiah tries to escape but is caught in the plains of Jericho, then is taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah, “where he gave judgment upon him.”

The city is destroyed, the city is annihilated, and thousands of Jews are taken out of their homeland. Habakkuk was left in the homeland because he was poor; he was a poor prophet.

Look at the judgment that happened to Zedekiah. The king of Babylon “slew the sons of Zedekiah” “before his eyes”: he killed his sons right in front of his face. He “slew all the nobles of Judah.” Then he “put out Zedekiah’s eyes”, took out his eyes, and “bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon.” That was the judgment.

The Chaldeans “burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem.” This was the final judgment. This is what Jeremiah warned Zedekiah of, but the people would not listen. It is the same message we tell our people today, and they don’t want to listen. Babylon annihilated our people, and Babylon the Great annihilated our people: America, during slavery.

Toward the ending chapters of Jeremiah, chapters 45 through 51, come the prophecies against each country: Moab’s judgment, Ammon’s judgment, Egypt’s judgment, Damascus’ judgment, the judgment that came on the countries surrounding Israel. God used Nebuchadnezzar to bring judgment to those countries, and some of those prophecies have a double meaning.

precepts.why:
This shows a little of what America did to us. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem”, who said raze it, “even to the foundation thereof.” Edom assisted the Babylonians in destroying Jerusalem. Remember, Edom is the Caucasian race.

“O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.” Edom stood with Babylon when Jerusalem was burned and its walls broken down, and the scripture says that daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed. What Edom did in the day of Jerusalem is what Edom did to our people again in America.

Our people did not believe this would happen, but it took place, and it is the same thing that happened to our people in the 1600s. God says “I will make this proverb to cease”, and “The days are at hand, and the effect of every vision”: what the prophets saw was coming to pass. “There shall be no more any vain vision” within the house of Israel.

This is the proverb God made to cease: “The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth.” A lot of Israelites didn’t believe it. They didn’t believe Moses: ‘no, that’s not gonna happen, that’s gonna fail, that’s not gonna take place.’ But it did.

The proof is the condition of our people today. We’re wasted, we’re destroyed, because we don’t even remember our true heritage.

sense.text:
“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee.” In Jeremiah’s time, Jeremiah knew he was a Jew; he knew he was an Israelite, even with Babylon destroying the land. So this verse has a double meaning.

Discontinuing from your heritage is the slave trade. It means we would not remember at all who we are. This is 1619, when they brought cargo slave ships with blacks and Hispanics. “And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: a strange land, under our enemies, “for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

This is to understand the current estate of our people. Jeremiah prophesied to our people that they would be destroyed by Babylon, and it happened; the same thing happened in America. Jeremiah 17 and Ezekiel 7 show how badly our people are messed up, and there are many more scriptures that say it.

precepts.why:
Watch how it describes the enemy we were caused to serve: “I will bring the worst of the heathen.” The Bible prophesies that God will bring the worst of the heathen, and this is Esau. “They shall possess their houses”, and “their holy places shall be defiled.”

The laughing barrel shows what the worst of the heathen did. On many plantations slaves were not allowed to laugh; we weren’t even allowed to be seen having fun. Slaves with boisterous personalities, wanting to laugh, often had to stifle their outbursts by the use of the laughing barrel. It was not by choice; this is what they were trained to do on the plantation. Some plantation owners had barrels set up, and when a slave heard something funny he would have to run off to one of those barrels in order to laugh, then go back to whatever he was doing. Some believe that is where the phrase ‘a barrel of laughs’ comes from.

The black house of praise also used shouting barrels when the slaves would steal away at night to church service. The slaves stifled the noises they wanted to make by holding their heads over barrels, sometimes filled with water, to keep the slave patrols and their white plantation owners from hearing them. White people viewed slaves laughing as a form of disrespect to them. Look at this, Esau: the white man viewed slaves laughing as disrespect. This is your good friendly neighborhood white man, four or five generations ago. It was not that long ago.

They don’t teach this in school; you have to find it doing research. It was shown at the Lest We Forget slavery museum, which had a laughing barrel just like it. There is so much history of the slave trade coming out that they did not discuss, and the Edomite teaching the slave trade and cotton in a high school class rushed through that section. This is what Ezekiel talked about when he said, I will bring the worst of the heathen: we weren’t even allowed to laugh.

This is proof that the state of our people right now is what all the nations wanted to see, and why we are still being oppressed. “All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee”; they hiss and gnash the teeth, and they say, We have swallowed her up: “certainly this is the day that we looked for.” The day that blacks and Hispanics would fall. “We have found, we have seen it.”

This is what Babylon the Great did when they destroyed us. Deuteronomy 28, Lamentations 5, Jeremiah 17:4 and Lamentations 2:16 all describe it, down to the laughing barrel during slavery.

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel”: this is Esau. Esau has had a perpetual hatred and has shed our blood on U.S. soil, “by the force of the sword”, “in the time of their calamity”, in the time of our calamity. And look at this part: “in the time that their iniquity had an end.” When our iniquity should have had an end, they said no. After the chains came off, it started the Jim Crow era.

The Moynihan report shows how deep this goes. Daniel Patrick Moynihan was an American politician, sociologist and diplomat, a Democrat who represented New York in the United States Senate and advised President Richard Nixon. His document came out in 1965 and was not meant to be seen by the public, but it got leaked: ‘The Negro Family: The Case for National Action.’ It says the black family structure is so destroyed that if action is not taken now it is only going to get worse. Angela Davis was upset at it, saying it blamed black people for their problems, and a lot of civil rights leaders did not like it. The document mainly deals with the tribe of Judah, how badly destroyed the tribe of Judah is; it deals with the northern kingdom only briefly.

It focused on the deep roots of black poverty and concluded that the high rate of families headed by single mothers would greatly hinder the progress of blacks toward economic and political equality. Moynihan argued that the rise in black single-mother families was caused not by a lack of jobs but by a destructive vein in ghetto culture that could be traced to slavery times and continued discrimination in the American South under Jim Crow. He got a lot of those ideas from E. Franklin Frazier, a black sociologist who introduced the idea in the 1930s. Right now during the protests, what do we want? Equality, to stop police brutality, to stop oppression. But it’s not just the police.

Its most controversial chapter is ‘the tangle of pathology’: middle-class black parents, father and mother with good jobs, do their best to get their child out of the projects, and the child, who could take his education to a higher level and excel, wants to sell drugs and be like what he sees on TV. It is like crabs in a barrel: you think you’re getting somewhere, and you come right back down.

The prologue says ‘the United States is approaching a new crisis in race relations.’ It’s 2020, and we are still having a crisis in race relations, because God said these two would not be united; he separated them. It says the expectations of the Negro Americans would go beyond civil rights, that equal opportunities would produce roughly equal results, and then that this will not happen, ‘nor will it happen for generations to come.’ He wrote that in 1965, and we are still protesting in 2020. Some say the document is damn near prophetic, but Esau thinks deep, and the Bible foretold all of this thousands of years ago. The report is only a reference to show that Esau understands it: its reasons are the racist virus in the American bloodstream, and three centuries of sometimes unimaginable mistreatment that have taken their toll. That is why we are always in the street.

sense.text:
Reading the 1965 report on the Negro family, it says ‘individually Negro Americans reach the highest peaks of achievement’. That’s your Jesse Owens, all these different celebrities, LeBron James, Floyd Mayweather. Psalms 87 is the scripture that goes with that individual, and to get the full thought we jump to verse 1: “His foundation is in the holy mountains.”

“The Lord loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.” When you really go into that verse, the Most High is saying he loves Judah more than all other tribes. But the Most High loves Israel.

In Psalms 87 the sons of Korah are speaking about the other nations: they’ve got great men born out of other nations, great men come out of there. Now it gets to Israel: “And of Zion it shall be said, This and that man was born in her: and the highest himself shall establish her.” Meaning in Israel, great people come out of here.
“The Lord shall count, when he writeth up the people, that this man was born there.” Who’s that? Jesus Christ.

“As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there”. Out of all the races, the best singers come out of blacks, Hispanics, Jamaicans, Native Americans. Think about it: the Harlem Renaissance, that was all Judah, that jazz music. God says when it comes to music, the best will come from my people.

“All my springs are in thee”: that’s the part we wanted. God says all my blessings are in thee. That’s why that report says individually Negro Americans reached the highest peaks of achievement: the blessing is in us. All we have to do is focus and tap into that nature and we will be great. Now us, repenting as Israelites, we want to be great for the Most High. But even some of our people that are not in the truth: Michael Jordan, there’s no basketball player like him, the blessing is in him. Barry Bonds, he’s Judah. Alex Rodriguez. All these individuals.

Those are just a few people compared to millions of us. The next sentence of the report says ‘but collectively’, among all the American ethnic and religious and regional groups, where some send their children to college and others pull them out of school at the eighth grade, ‘Negroes are among the weakest’. So this Edomite was saying when it comes to black people as a nation, they are at the bottom, but individually they are at the top.

Just like Babylon annihilated the temple and our people, the Bible said it would be worse for our people with Deuteronomy 28, what America would do. The report’s chapter on the roots of the problem starts with slavery, Deuteronomy 28, and the question ‘why was American slavery the most awful the world has ever known?’

In the street when we’re teaching, people say, oh, everybody been through slavery. Shut up. What the hell is wrong with you? American slavery is the worst, because blacks were reduced to chattels.

“What thing shall I take to witness for thee?” “That I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion”. Exactly: what can I compare to thee? Because nobody went through what we went through.

Esau understands it: in 1965 that report said the Negro family, battered and harassed by discrimination, injustice and uprooting, is in the deepest trouble. The family structure has been destroyed, and all of it is the result of Deuteronomy 28. That’s why we are dangerous individuals, and why Esau is trying to put a media blackout on Israel: we have the power to fix families, because we’re using God’s laws.

Remember Jeremiah was prophesying, saying listen, evil’s coming. Now we’re going to show you evil’s coming, but the reason a lot of our people won’t listen is because of these few scriptures: it’s the leaders. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” These political leaders are causing our people to err. Sharpton is set up to keep our people calm; that’s what he’s for. He’s a vessel used by America.

precepts.why:
“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement”. Our people think there’s got to be a way we can be equal, we can be equal with you, we can join with you. No, that’s you making a covenant with hell and death, and it’s only going to get you death. We have to join with the Most High. You need to join with IUIC, because we’re going to teach you right.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge”. What you’ve made your comfort: white Jesus. ‘I’m going to be an upright citizen’: that’s your comfort. ‘I’m going to vote and everything’s going to be alright’: that’s your comfort. It’s not going to work.

For too long, black men and black women, you’ve been trying to fix the American system. How can you fix this system when it was built off of slavery? There’s no fixing it. The Most High used Esau to beat our backs; you can’t fix him. There’s only one way out: we have to join to the Lord, we have to join with the Most High, we have to repent. Otherwise it’s “under falsehood have we hid ourselves”.

“Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter”. It’s the leaders seducing our people, crying peace where there is none.

We’re going to hit it where it hurts: it’s the leaders, the leaders are causing our people to err. That’s why you need to join the movement, join Israel United in Christ, and help us fix our people and teach our people repentance. You at home watching this, this is your call.

“Why do the heathen rage”: why are all the other nations upset? “And the people imagine a vain thing”: they really believe they can stop this truth. “The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying, Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.”

“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”. You will listen to everybody except the Israelites. The counsel we’re giving you is the counsel of the Bible, what God says. But our people say, let’s see what these political leaders got. No, let’s see what God has to say.

“And that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”: the covering is our people joining with the American political system, “that they may add sin to sin.” Under American politics, whether you’re Republican or Democrat, conservative, whatever it is, you can still be a homosexual, you can still be a lesbian. Joining that is not going to help you repent of your sins at all; it’s a covering, but not of God’s spirit.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh”: strengthening yourselves in the strength of the American economy, the American political system, “and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” America is not literally Egypt, but it’s the shadow of Egypt. When you’re walking you see your shadow; it isn’t literally you, it’s just a figure. America is the shadow of Egypt.

“Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame”: the strength of the American political system shall be your shame. If you really believe voting is what’s going to save the black man, it’s only going to be your shame. Black people since slavery have always had the same message: we want liberty, we want freedom. “And the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.”
